page_title: OTTO boosts forecasting accuracy up to 30%  with Google Cloud's TiDE and Vertex AI Innovations

team_name_team_lumen.sentence: OTTO’s forecasting team, Team Lumen, implemented Google Cloud’s advanced AI tools, including Vertex AI, BigQuery, and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), to achieve this.

tide_model.sentence: The integration of the Time-series Dense Encoder (TiDE) model revolutionized their demand prediction capabilities.
tide_model.also: The Time-series Dense Encoder (TiDE), trained on Vertex AI and deployed on GKE, has enabled OTTO to improve the accuracy of demand forecasts by up to 30%.

gke.sentence: OTTO’s forecasting team, Team Lumen, implemented Google Cloud’s advanced AI tools, including Vertex AI, BigQuery, and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), to achieve this.

up_to_30_percent_accuracy_improvement.sentence: The adoption of Google’s solutions resulted in an up to 30% improvement in forecasting accuracy, reduced inventory costs, and increased customer satisfaction through timely product availability.
up_to_30_percent_accuracy_improvement.also_headline: OTTO boosts forecasting accuracy up to 30%  with Google Cloud's TiDE and Vertex AI Innovations

up_to_30_percent_accuracy_improvement.also_body: The Time-series Dense Encoder (TiDE), trained on Vertex AI and deployed on GKE, has enabled OTTO to improve the accuracy of demand forecasts by up to 30%.

seasonal_inventory.sentence: For example, when planning seasonal inventory for gaming consoles, TiDE’s advanced architecture delivers highly accurate predictions by capturing short- and long-term dependencies.

notes: [Certain] Every individual claim element (team name, TiDE, Vertex AI, BigQuery, GKE, an up-to-30% accuracy figure, seasonal inventory) is stated verbatim somewhere on the page, each with an exact supporting sentence quoted above.

[Certain] The README's specific composite framing -- 'put a Time-series Dense Encoder (TiDE) model on Vertex AI, BigQuery and GKE' -- is a compression the page itself does not state as one sentence. The page's closest sentence lists Vertex AI, BigQuery and GKE as the tools Team Lumen implemented generally, and a separate sentence says TiDE specifically was 'trained on Vertex AI and deployed on GKE' (no BigQuery in that sentence). BigQuery's own stated role vis-a-vis TiDE is as a data source ('extract historical product sales data from BigQuery and use it in Vertex AI to train forecasting models'), not as a system TiDE is described as running 'on'. This is a minor overclaim/compression in the README's phrasing, not a fabrication -- all three products are genuinely part of the same stack per the page, just not tied to TiDE specifically as a trio in one sentence.

[Certain] 'up to 30%' is the page's own headline and repeated figure (also written once as a flat 'by 30%' without 'up to', in the intro paragraph). 'Seasonal inventory' appears on the page as a specific worked example (gaming consoles) rather than the subject of the 30% figure itself -- the page never states the 30% improvement was specifically 'for seasonal inventory'; the README's clause 'for seasonal inventory' pairs two facts the page keeps in separate sentences.

[Certain] The page never uses the word 'measured' for the 30% figure (README says 'measured up to a 30% improvement'); the page's own verbs are 'resulted in', 'enabled ... to improve', and 'improve ... by'. Not treated as a meaningful discrepancy, just noted for completeness.

[Certain] No mention anywhere on the page of BigQuery AI.FORECAST, TimesFM, or ARIMA_PLUS_XREG -- the README's own framing of this citation as production evidence for 'this project's own choice of stack (BigQuery AI.FORECAST/ARIMA_PLUS_XREG on Vertex)' is the README's inference/analogy, not something the OTTO page itself draws; the page describes TiDE on Vertex AI/BigQuery/GKE only.
